reasons: Both answers propose nearly identical server-authoritative architectures (shared config, server cooldown, type checks, server raycast with pellet aggregation) and meet every rubric item. B adds a clearer today-vs-should-be table, spells out the hybrid client-hit validation (distance, position tolerance, LOS raycast) the rubric describes, and covers extra practical points (self-hit exclusion, team check, server-side ammo, replicating tracers). A is slightly tighter on NaN handling and per-weapon cooldowns, but B's broader concrete guidance serves the user a bit better.
